scope: Measurement and continue decision only; application source and PDFium rendering unchanged.
method: Release x64, same executable/DLLs, fresh isolated settings, 900x1000 window, warm OS file cache, hidden app PDBs. One PDF opened from an empty window, waited for render idle, sampled after 1 s, closed and sampled after 1 s. Independent 200 ms host/target CPU and memory monitor. Engine order alternated.
limits: Document open from an already running empty window, not process startup or first paint. Whole-process Private Bytes do not identify allocation owners. Single-page, one-tab snapshots; no long-lived session. Third PDF has no qualifying pair. Prior first-page phase timings came from Debug diagnostics, not these Release runs.

gate.start: Three consecutive 1 s samples with busy CPU <=10% and OS memory load <=85%
gate.row: Other-CPU mean <=10%, p95 <=20% over 200 ms samples, OS memory load <=90%
gate.pair: Starting OS memory load within 3 percentage points

exclusions: Two BERT and two IPA pairs exceeded background CPU limits. The final IPA attempt timed out after 60 s without three quiet start samples; no IPA pair qualified.
attribution: Prior Debug phase trace: attention first-page load 368.8 ms versus bitmap rendering 8.9 ms; raster first-page load 2.1 ms. Font matching is plausible, not proven. Prior four-document Private Bytes 80.8 MiB empty, 153.1 MiB visited; known cached pixel payload 23.1 MiB, leaving about 49 MiB unassigned. Current one-document PDFium memory returns within 0.2-0.5 MiB of empty after close.
decision: Continue targeted diagnosis. Do not adopt font-info v2 or change cache policy; font-info v2 changes alias text pixels. No optimization implemented or approved.
next: Measure direct process launch under the same load gates; profile first-page and font lookup in Release for independent text PDFs; attribute non-pixel memory by cache/GDI/SDK ownership; require matching PDFium text pixels including aliases and Japanese glyphs before any font-path change.
